solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Chaos often associated with Eton?

blocks.note: the word that follows Eton in the name of a summer pudding of meringue, cream and strawberries

explanation.surface: A dig at the rowdiness of the famous boys' school.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is a public school, so the surface suggests misbehaving pupils; the second half is really the English dessert Eton mess.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for disorder in one sense, and in the other the second word of the dessert named after the school.

clue.text: Staff assume Alexander’s home

blocks.note: a mace is a ceremonial staff
to don is to put on, assume

explanation.surface: Staff take up residence in a great man's house.
explanation.walkthrough: Alexander is Alexander the Great; the surface makes him sound like an employer with a household.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by allusion: the ancient Greek kingdom where Alexander the Great was born and became king.

clue.text: Raised taxes irritate City

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word that is raised reads from the bottom up, so it is written backwards

blocks.note: VAT is value added tax; VATS are taxes

explanation.surface: Tax rises annoy the financial City.
explanation.walkthrough: "City" seems to be the City of London, where tax news matters; it is the definition, a port in Norway.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Stavanger is one city among many, the oil capital of south-west Norway.

clue.text: Teaching system — fools can get transformed with it

indicators.note: things that are transformed change their form, so the letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A method of teaching so good that even fools are changed by it.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes in "it" as well as "fools can"; "with" is what adds it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sight-singing method taught with do, re, mi syllables, so a system for teaching music.

clue.text: Queer fish, it is eaten by seabird taking the head off

indicators.note: what is eaten ends up inside the eater
a word's head is its first letter, and taking it off removes that letter

blocks.note: NODDY, a tropical tern, without its N

explanation.surface: A seabird swallows a fish, head first.
explanation.walkthrough: "Fish" belongs to the definition, not the wordplay: a queer fish is an odd person. The noddy is a tern, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a queer fish is an eccentric person, someone peculiar.

clue.text: Popular golf cancelled in the US over wage fixing system

indicators.note: turned over means upside down, so in a down clue the word is written from the bottom up

blocks.note: to nix is American slang for to cancel
G is golf in the radio alphabet; it sits under the reversed word

explanation.surface: A popular round of golf is scrapped in America because of a pay dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: "in the US" flags that the synonym is American.
explanation.definitionFit: Tying pay rises to a price index such as inflation is a system for setting wages.

clue.text: Exhausted with strain after minutes in function — it takes gall to keep working

definitions.text: it takes gall to keep working

indicators.note: coming after something means following it
being in something means inside it

blocks.note: a strain on something tests it
the trigonometric function, wrapped around the rest as S…INE

explanation.surface: A worn-out worker admires the nerve needed to carry on.
explanation.walkthrough: Gall means cheek in the surface but bile in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: bile (gall) from the gall bladder drains into this part of the gut, which needs it to digest fats.

clue.text: One accommodated by fat landowner

indicators.note: a guest accommodated by a host lives inside the host's house

blocks.note: lard is pig fat, split as LA…RD
I = one, the Roman numeral; goes inside

explanation.surface: A guest put up by a portly country squire.
explanation.walkthrough: A laird is a Scottish landed proprietor.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional word: Scots for the owner of a landed estate.

clue.text: Prevaricated, not wanting page changed

indicators.note: to be wanting something is to lack it

explanation.surface: Someone who dodged the truth did not want a page amended.
explanation.walkthrough: Palter is an uncommon word for shifting and equivocating; the definition is at the end, not "Prevaricated".
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something modified has been made different.

clue.text: Happy with opening in good time

blocks.note: as in the early, opening stages

explanation.surface: Someone is pleased to open their shop punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: "with" is not a link word here but a piece of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for arriving at the start of the day, ahead of time.

clue.text: Cleaner embarrassed how the settee got very close to the fire?

definitions.text: how the settee got very close to the fire?

blocks.note: a char, or charwoman, is a cleaning lady

explanation.surface: A cleaner is mortified at the scorched sofa.
explanation.walkthrough: Char is dated British for a woman hired to clean houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: furniture left too near the flames ends up scorched and blackened.

clue.text: Writer is entertained by papers lying about literature?

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is taken into the host's home
lying about, like lying around, means turned round

explanation.surface: A writer is kept amused by newspapers that lie about books.
explanation.walkthrough: The ? acknowledges that literature as ART is a loose equation.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: someone who keeps a journal is one kind of writer.

clue.text: A stuffed sausage which will stop you getting wind?

definitions.text: A stuffed sausage which will stop you getting wind?

blocks.note: not food: a long padded fabric tube, often shaped like a dog

blocks.clueFragment: which will stop you getting wind?
blocks.note: not indigestion: the wind is cold air under the door

explanation.surface: A sausage said to prevent flatulence.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as food and indigestion, but the sausage is a stuffed cloth roll laid along the bottom of a door.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description of the household object that blocks a cold draught, described by its shape and job.

clue.text: Dark times with no lights with oil heartlessly withheld

indicators.note: a word's heart is its middle letter
letters withheld are kept back, so O and L are taken out

blocks.note: OIL without its centre; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A blackout because the lamp oil has run out.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters removed are the O after N and the L before I.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours of darkness between dusk and dawn are the dark times of each day.

clue.text: One French knight competed, making no one resentful

definitions.note: adjective phrase: unenvied is a state that leaves no one resentful

blocks.note: N is the knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: A French knight enters a tournament and nobody minds.
explanation.walkthrough: Knight is N, not K, because K is already the king in chess notation.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose paraphrase: if your lot provokes no jealousy, nobody resents you for it.

clue.text: I can time railway travel plan

blocks.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone boasts they can time a rail journey.
explanation.walkthrough: "can" looks like a verb but is the noun, a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the planned route and schedule of a journey.

clue.text: Ingredient used in cosmetic salon stripped several bare

indicators.note: stripping takes off the outer covering
laid bare means uncovered

explanation.surface: At a beauty salon, several customers are waxed bare.
explanation.walkthrough: "Ingredient used in cosmetic salon" wants to be one phrase; the definition stops at "cosmetic".
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the soothing plant gel is a common component of skin creams.

clue.text: Doctor originally learnt about in outskirts of Hull

indicators.note: moved about means rearranged
being in something means inside it, so the anagram sits within H…L
a town's outskirts are its edges

blocks.note: first and last letters, wrapped around the rest

explanation.surface: A doctor first studied around the edges of Hull.
explanation.walkthrough: "originally" looks like a first-letter signal for "learnt"; it belongs to the definition. Hull is a city in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivia: William Hartnell was the first actor to play the Doctor in the BBC's Doctor Who, from 1963.

clue.text: Cannabis and heroin the man’s hidden in tree

blocks.note: belonging to him; inside the tree

explanation.surface: A man stashes cannabis and heroin in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: "hidden" does not signal a hidden word here; it is a container, and H for heroin is standard drug slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: hashish is the resin form of the drug cannabis.

clue.text: Call into question feminine credo

blocks.note: to belie is to contradict or show to be false

explanation.surface: Someone challenges a feminist creed.
explanation.walkthrough: Belie also means to give a false impression, but here it is to cast doubt on.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: credo is Latin for 'I believe', the opening word of the creed.

clue.text: Healthy types beginning on training equipment

indicators.note: a word's beginning is its first letter

explanation.surface: Fit people start using gym kit.
explanation.walkthrough: "training equipment" reads as one phrase; it splits, with "equipment" alone the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a fixed piece of furniture or apparatus in a room.

clue.text: Gang member that is under court?

indicators.note: in a down clue, what is under something is written below it

explanation.surface: A gangster ends up before a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: "under court" suggests facing trial; it is positional.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional term: in Britain and Jamaica the word names a member of a Jamaican criminal gang.

clue.text: Foreign ministry reported European new in role came across

indicators.note: being in something means inside it

blocks.note: n = new; inside MET to give MENT

explanation.surface: A news report about a new European taking up a post at a foreign ministry.
explanation.walkthrough: "in role" suggests a job, but "in" puts N inside MET.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the American government body that runs foreign affairs.

clue.text: Scotsman’s gone from 1990s dance scene

indicators.note: what has gone from a place is no longer in it

blocks.note: the Macarena, a 1990s novelty dance hit
Mac is a stock name for a Scot; removed

explanation.surface: A Scot has left the 90s dance scene.
explanation.walkthrough: "dance scene" reads as one phrase; "scene" alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: a sphere of activity, as in the political one.

clue.text: Like a good port in winter, not very chilled

definitions.text: Like a good port in winter

blocks.clueFragment: Like a good port in winter
blocks.note: a harbour that stays open when the sea freezes
a drink served with nothing in the glass to cool it

explanation.surface: A glass of port for winter, served not too cold.
explanation.walkthrough: The port is a harbour, not the fortified wine the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Two literal senses: a harbour kept open all winter, and a drink served without cubes to cool it.

clue.text: Hero showing what it took to make his name?

definitions.text: Hero showing what it took to make his name?

blocks.note: a comic-strip hero, not a real one

blocks.clueFragment: showing what it took to make his name?
blocks.note: not how he became famous, but the word inside his surname: courage

explanation.surface: A hero whose reputation came from his courage.
explanation.walkthrough: Dan Dare, Pilot of the Future, was a British comic-strip space hero from the Eagle; his surname literally names the boldness heroes need.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the British space hero's name spells out the daring that makes a name.

clue.text: Considerable brilliance which is used in moderation?

blocks.note: the water of a diamond is its lustre, as in 'of the first water'

explanation.surface: Great talent that should be used sparingly.
explanation.walkthrough: Moderation sounds like restraint, but in a nuclear reactor a moderator slows neutrons.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: deuterium oxide slows neutrons as the moderator in some nuclear reactors.

clue.text: Returned to the old island

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters read from the end

blocks.note: ye is the old form of 'the', as in Ye Olde Shoppe

explanation.surface: Someone came back to an old island.
explanation.walkthrough: The word, also spelt ait, is common on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional word: English for a small island in a river.
